summary: Joanna Macy (1929–2025) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Wellesley College (~1946–1950) and Syracuse University (~1973–1978), and later taught Stephanie Kaza and Doug Kraft.

Joanne Punzo Waghorne specializes in religious studies and Indology. After studying at the University of Chicago, she held positions at the University of Massachusetts Boston (1975–1983), Bowdoin College (1983–1985), UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University (from 2002; attested 2014).

Joe Bransford Wilson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Virginia (Ph.D. 1984), taught at Virginia (1981–1985), and served at the University of North Carolina Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

Joe Cribb (born 1947) is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of London and Queen Mary University (~1967–1970), he served as Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1970–2010).

Joel Peter Brereton (born 1948) works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Stanley Insler in 1971 and held posts at the University of Missouri (1999–2000) and the University of Texas at Austin (from 2004, emeritus ~2020).
Joel Tatelman is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford in 1996 under the supervision of Alexis Sanderson.
Joen Imai is a scholar of Buddhist studies who has served as a professor at Shuchiin University (attested in 2010 and 2026).

Joerg Tuske specializes in philosophy and Indology. He held a post at the University of Cambridge (attested 1998) and served as an associate professor of philosophy at Salisbury University (attested 2013).

Joey Hung (born 1991) works in computational fields and Buddhist studies. After attending the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts, he held a post at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (~2014) and later at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Jogendra Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Uma Shankar Vyas at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Jogindra Nath Samaddar (1884–1929) was an Indologist and historian educated at Bangabasi College and Presidency University. He taught at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College (~1908–1917), Patna College (1912), and Patna University (1923).

Johan Elverskog (born 1968) works in Buddhist, religious, and Central Asian studies. Educated at UC Berkeley (B.A. ~1989–1993) and Indiana University Bloomington (M.A. ~1993–1995), he became the Dedman Family Distinguished Professor at Southern Methodist University (~2002).

Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern (1833–1917) was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Utrecht, Leiden (doctorate 1855), and under Albrecht Weber, he taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1863–1865) and held the Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1865–1903).
Johan Hendrik Kern (1867–1933) was a linguist. He held academic posts at the University of Groningen (1901–1924) and Leiden University (1924–1933).

Johan Huizinga (1872–1945) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Groningen (~1891–1895) and Leiden University (~1895–1896) under J. H. C. Kern, later teaching at Groningen (1905–1915) and Leiden (1914–1942).

Johann Andreas Schmeller (1785–1852) studied at the University of Munich (~1801–1803). He served at the Bavarian Cadet Corps (~1817–1826), the Bavarian State Library (from 1829), and held a professorship in Old German language and literature at the University of Munich (1828; 1846).

Johann Caspar von Orelli (1787–1849) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He held academic appointments at the Cantonal School of Graubünden (~1807–1819), Carolinum Zürich (~1819–1833), and the University of Zurich (~1833–1849).

Johann Christoph Adelung (1732–1806) was a linguist who studied at the Kloster Berge school (~1746–1752) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1752). He taught at Evangelisches Ratsgymnasium Erfurt (1758) and served as chief librarian at Dresden (1787).

Johann Friedrich Blumenbach (1752–1840) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the universities of Jena (~1769–1772) and Göttingen (~1772–1775), where he subsequently held a post from ~1775 to 1840.
Johann Friedrich Herbart (1776–1841) was a philosopher. He studied at the University of Jena (~1794–1797) and held a post at the University of Göttingen (~1802–1809).
